Librogame.title: Suddenly an Ogre
Librogame.author: J. Alan Henning

Changes.Change: Rewritten for this engine; the numbered entries and their choices are unchanged

The arrows no longer promise a count. The original contradicts itself — one arrow in the instructions, three in the list at entry 14 — and nothing here counts ammunition: how many are left is something the story tells you
The gem worth four hundred coins is a real item now. You find it on the ogre's body, it stays in your pack, and the two endings that speak of it are the two you can only reach carrying it

Two of the six things you could work out from the tree gave the same answer — that it finds you by ear and nose, not by sight. They are now one, and the entry that had lost every way in is gone, as the author did with his own entries 86 and 154
What the text says you lose, you really lose: the sword you abandon, the bow the club tears from your hands, the armour the ogre strips from you while you are out cold. Twenty-six places in all

Entry 62 has a third way out, which the original does not have: at that entry you can only offer the sword or the bow, and a reader who no longer has either would have been left with no button at all. Showing your empty hands to a goddess of war ends the way it ends
The prologue is back where the original has it, at the head of the first entry: without it you would start running without knowing why
Entry 4 asked the reader to put a question to a game master; here it is six things the character tries to work out from the branch

Entries 46 and 136 asked the reader to remember whether the potion had been given away. The potion now really leaves the inventory when you offer it or leave it behind, and the book reads the inventory instead of asking
A handful of choice labels were harmonised: five ways of saying «run» where two are enough
The Dungeon World move names and the pre-rolled dice are gone: here the book reads as a story, not as a lesson in a game system
The damage the original narrated is now real. You start with 18 hit points, as the original character does, and the numbers taken from you are the ones the author wrote scene by scene
At entry 155 the damage is 4 instead of 5: on the one route that reaches it, the original's arithmetic leaves the reader at 1 hit point, and the scenes before it spend one more
Three rolls that depended on the weight or value of what you carry became explicit choices, because this engine cannot add up an inventory into a die roll
Where the original really asks you to roll — eleven places — the app rolls for you
The book declares no abilities and no skills, because no scene reads any; the load counter is gone, because no scene changed it
The inventory grid tracking seven separate playthroughs is not included: it belongs to paper
Entries 86 and 154 of the original, which nothing points to, are left out
The scenes have no titles, as in the original: a heading above a scene would say what is about to happen
Cover photograph not included; its source is not stated in the original

Librogame.Blurb:
Your sister is dying. The healer gave you the potion and told you that time is everything: the long way round will get you home too late, and the forest path is not safe. You take the forest path.
Two hours in, you hear branches breaking. What comes out of the pines is eight feet tall, carries a tree trunk, and is not always in the mood to talk. Eighteen hit points, a hundred and fifty-eight scenes, seventeen endings — and some of them are not the one you would call winning.
Librogame.ContentWarnings: Violence, gore, death, and disappointing a parent.

Page.Text:
You ran through the afternoon and night across the grasslands, circumventing the dark wood, and reached the healer's hut at noon.
Breathlessly you explained your sister's illness. The healer gave you a healing potion but emphasized that time is vital. If you go back the roundabout way you came, your sister will be dead when you arrive. The forest path is not safe, but it is most direct. It's your one chance of saving her.
You have rushed along the forest path for two hours. Suddenly you hear branches breaking not far from you, and the muffled sound of heavy footsteps on fallen pine needles. You can’t see anything between the dense pines. The narrow path through the dark wood continues to the north.
What do you do?

Choice.text: Run back along the path south, trying not to make any noise
Climb a pine tree behind you for a better look
Wait until whatever it is comes closer

Page.Text:
As you quickly turn to run back along the path, you trip over a root and fall beside the path into pine needles, your belt tearing, sending your sheathed sword flying. Looking behind you see a small head high up, poking above branches.
What do you do?

Choice.text: Roll into the brush and remain motionless
Grab your scabbard, unsheathe your sword, and stand ready
Abandon your sword, leap up and rush south down the path

Page.Text:
You hear the creature coming closer, moving quickly through the underbrush. Suddenly a small head, high up, pokes above the trees, stopping just short of the path. Clearly it is a large creature, perhaps eight feet tall. It sniffs the air, then looks directly at you. Its eyes grow wide, and it strides onto the path. It’s a monstrous naked humanoid, about eight-feet tall, with a small head. In one hand it holds a section of tree trunk, like a club.
What do you do?

Choice.text: Try to remember all you know about such creatures
Notch an arrow to your bow and shoot it
Make conversation with it

Page.Text:
Climbing the pine tree, you pull yourself up onto a thick limb. Your hands are sticky with pine sap, and the pleasant aroma of the pine almost lulls you into a sense of comfort. But you see movement among the pines, and you can’t make out what it is. As it moves closer, you see that it is a monstrously large creature, perhaps eight feet tall, but with a small head. An ogre! It carries a section of tree trunk at its side, like a club.
From up here, what do you try to work out?

Choice.text: Look for what has passed through here
Watch it, to see what it is about to do
Work out what you should be watching for
Look around for anything that could help you
Look harder, in case it is not what it seems

Page.Text:
From the tree you see deep footprints across the path, leading into the thickness on the other side of the path, where you can now see branches that were broken. The ogre must have traveled from that part of the forest.
You look back down at the ogre and see its nostrils are flared wide. It must have caught your smell, and it is moving its head back and forth scanning the treetops. It looks right up at you and roars, a bestial sound that echoes through the forest and scares crows into flight, their caws drowning out its roar.
The ogre rushes towards the base of your tree.
What do you do?

Choice.text: Climb higher into the tree
Notch an arrow to your bow and try to shoot the ogre

Page.Text:
Clearly this is a large creature, perhaps eight feet tall, only its small head poking above the pine branches. It sniffs the air, then looks directly at you. Its eyes grow wide, and it strides into the path. It’s a monstrous naked humanoid, about eight-feet tall, with that disproportionately small head. In one hand it holds a section of tree trunk, like a club, which it begins swinging in front of it like a scythe.
What do you do?

Choice.text: Try to evade the tree trunk and dart in close to the ogre
Retreat into the pine trees, defending yourself as you do so

Page.Text:
The creature is sniffing the air, its nostrils flaring wide. Most likely it is about to catch your scent.
What do you do?

Choice.text: Climb higher into the tree
Climb down from the tree and run
Stay motionless in the hope that it doesn’t discover where you are

Page.Text:
It’s clearly an ogre. The head is human, because ogres once were humans, humans who hid in the deep woods. There they grew to loathe their ancestors. On the hills above the forests they built crude stone altars and sacrificed deer and bears to dark gods, until they grew in stature but not wisdom and began to sacrifice humans to their dark gods as well.
You guess you picked this up from bits of songs the bards sing in taverns.
What do you do?

Choice.text: Notch an arrow to your bow and shoot it
Make conversation with it

Page.Text:
The small-headed creature has big ears and large flaring nostrils, but gleaming little eyes. It’s more likely to hear you or smell you than it is to see you, up in this tree.
What do you do?

Choice.text: Throw pine cones deep into the woods to draw the monster’s attention
Stay motionless in the hope that it doesn’t discover where you are
Scurry down the tree on the other side and hide among the leaves, twigs, and pine cones at its base, so that it won’t be able to smell you

Page.Text:
You rush down the path, as fast and quietly as you can. Fortunately, the path turns and twists, and you are out of sight of the creature. You hear no signs that you are being followed.
What do you want to do?

Choice.text: Hide off the trail for a while, then return to get your sword
Retrace your steps back along the path, hoping the ogre has gone
Try to cut through the forest towards home, at the risk of getting lost

Page.Text:
From the tree top, you can see that the trail bends to the east. You can cut through the woods in a straight line and rejoin the trail further on.
You look from the pine cones on the branches near you back down to the large ears of the monster.
What do you want to do?

Choice.text: Throw pine cones deep into the woods to draw the monster’s attention
Climb back down and dart through the forest east and try to rejoin the trail further on

Page.Text: The arrow is nocked. From here, though, the shot is not there yet.

Choice.text: Move until you can see it clearly, even if that means being seen
Loose the arrow from where you stand and take what you get
Empty the quiver at it, and worry about that afterwards

Page.Text:
“Hello, there,” you say, “don’t mind me. I’m just walking through the woods. I’ll be out of your way in a moment.”
“You pay toll,” the creature says, in a raspy voice, surprisingly soft for its size. Its eyes are red.
You try to think about what you have that this creature would value. Your armor is too small for it to wear. Your sword would be like a knife to it. Altogether you have:
Dungeon rations (5 uses, 1 weight; 3 coins)
Adventuring gear (1 weight; 20 coins)
Healing potion (0 weight; 50 coins)
Leather armor (1 armor, 1 weight; 10 coins)
3 coins (0 weight)
Short sword (close, 1 weight; 8 coins)
Worn bow (near, 2 weight; 15 coins)
Arrows (1 weight; 1 coin)
What do you do?

Choice.text: Which of these will you offer it? Make your decision
Keep your stuff. Notch an arrow to your bow and shoot it

Page.Text:
Nothing is not what it appears to be?!
It’s a big scary monster with a big scary stick, stomping through the forest looking for heads to smash.
Actually, its eyes are red, and it appears to have been crying.
What do you want to do?

Choice.text: Remain silent and motionless high in the tree until it passes by
Climb down the tree and talk with the ogre

Page.Text: The ogre comes near, and you hear its snuffling and shuffling. It’s not far from you. You wish you could wait for dusk but time is of the essence to save your sister. Finally it starts moving away. You wait until the stomps of the ogre have faded off into the distance. You cautiously, slowly, retrace your steps back to the general part of the trail where you left the sword.

Choice.text: You recall perfectly where you left it, right?
At the time, you memorized where you left it, right?

Page.Text:
You take a step forward, centering yourself in the path, and line up a series of clean shots. Two arrows thunk into the shoulder of the ogre, who howls in pain and rage. The third arrow zooms over its shoulder as it barrels down on you, moving surprisingly fast. The ogre is swinging its club at you.
What do you do?

Choice.text: Use your bow to defend yourself from taking the full force of the club
Try to roll under its swinging club to come close enough to stab it

Page.Text:
While you climbed higher, the ogre began violently shaking your tree. You are swaying back and forth, barely able to hold on.
What do you do?

Choice.text: Cling tightly to the tree so you don’t fall off to your death
Hold tightly to the tree but try to shoot the ogre with your bow

Page.Text:
You try to avoid the swinging club, but the monster is faster than it looks, and smashes you to the ground. You clamber back to your feet, your short sword ready.
What do you do?

Choice.text: Stab the monster
Make a fighting retreat into the woods

Page.Text: You try to think about what you have that this creature would value. The more it is worth, the better your chances that it lets you pass — and the less you will have if it does not.

Choice.text: Offer the healing potion, the most valuable thing you carry
Offer your adventuring gear
Offer your leather armour
Offer your worn bow
Show it your empty hands: you have given it everything already

Page.Text:
The dense branches of the tree, which made it so easy for you to climb, make it hard for you to line up a good shot.
Choose one:

Choice.text: You have to move to get the shot, coming close to the ogre
You have to take what you can get
You have to shoot again and again, until there is nothing left to shoot

Page.Text:
The sap of the pine tree is sticking to your hands as you try to hurry down.
What do you do?

Choice.text: Hurry so quickly that you end up falling the rest of the way
Go so cautiously that the ogre sniffs you and comes near

Page.Text:
You carefully pluck three pine cones from the nearest branch and, taking measured aim at a distant tree, hurl them as far as you can. The pine cones miss the tree you aimed for but one careens off a branch with a satisfying thunk.
The ogre lets out a roar and strides off towards the sound.
What do you do?

Choice.text: Descend the tree and run along the trail as fast as you can
Descend the tree and run through the woods as fast as you can, avoiding the trail

Page.Text:
You return to the trail but you don’t see your sword anywhere. You look carefully through the twigs, pine needles, and rotted leaves along the trail but fail to find it. To replace that sword will cost you at least eight silver coins, far more than the three coins you have.
What do you do?

Choice.text: Search along the trail for as long as it takes
Forget the sword and travel along the path

Page.Text:
Desperately you use your bow to try and stop the club from slamming down on you. The club breaks your bow and crushes your shoulder.
The ogre raises the club to strike again.
You drop your broken bow and draw your short sword. What do you do?

Choice.text: Try to evade the club and get in close

Page.Text:
Suddenly the nostrils of the ogre flare, and it raises its head, sniffing and snuffling. You carefully move along a branch, hiding behind the trunk of the tree, hoping it can’t see or smell you. But to your horror you hear it coming closer. It is beneath you now and has begun shaking the tree violently.
What do you do?

Choice.text: Cling tightly to the tree so you don’t fall off to your death
Hold tightly to the tree but try to shoot the ogre with your bow

Page.Text:
The ogre looms over you. You stab up towards its stomach, but the ogre wraps its huge hand around your swordhand, squeezing and breaking your fingers, then pulling the sword out of your hand. It drives your own sword into you, and you fall to the ground.
The ogre pulls out the sword and prepares to attack again, but you fall to the ground, apparently lifeless.

Shakingly, you hold out your hand with your offered toll.
The creature swings its tree-trunk club at you, smashing you to the ground in pain, sending your toll flying and injuring your swordhand.
“Not a good toll!” it shouts at you angrily. “Everything give me!” It menaces you with its club.
Your swordhand aches.
What do you do?

Choice.text: Place everything you have, everything, into a pile
Place some items into a pile, then run for it

Page.Text:
To get a good shot, you need to climb back down the tree a bit before you can fire. Your arrow drives deep into the ogre’s shoulder, and it lets out a howl.
What do you do?

Choice.text: Drop your bow and jump down on it, trying to kill it with your sword
Fire again

Page.Text:
As you hurry, you lose your footing and fall the rest of the way down the tree, careening off branches before hitting the ground.
What do you do?

Choice.text: Run back down the path the way you came, away from the ogre (and away from home)
Run through the woods as fast as you can, avoiding the trail

Page.Text:
You cannot see where the ogre has gone. If it is still near the trail, you probably have one shot at running past it, or risk being caught and eaten.
The more you carry, the slower you run. What are you willing to leave behind?

Choice.text: Nothing. Run with everything you have
The armour, the bow and the adventuring gear
Everything except the potion

Page.Text:
You curse the craftsmanship of the leather scabbard, which you were normally so proud of, but which now makes it harder to find. At last, you have it back in your hand. You can’t help but admire the filigree.
You hear the crunch of a branch breaking underfoot and see a monstrous naked humanoid bearing down upon you, its nostrils flaring. It is about eight-feet tall, with a disproportionately small head. In one hand it holds a section of tree trunk, like a club, which it begins swinging in front of it like a scythe.
What do you do?

Choice.text: Try to evade the tree trunk and dart in close to the ogre
Retreat into the pine trees, defending yourself as you do so

Page.Text:
You try to feint and lunge with your sword, but the ogre brings its club down on you and crushes you to the ground before you can even get near to it.
The ogre lets go off the tree trunk that it was using as a club; the club continues to press you to the ground. It seizes your short sword from your hand.
What do you do?

Choice.text: Play dead
Push the trunk off and run for it

Page.Text:
The ogre is shaking the tree so viciously that you fall slightly down the tree, banging your head against a branch.
What do you do?

Choice.text: Hold tightly to the tree but try to shoot the ogre with your bow
Try to climb higher up the widely swinging tree to stay out of reach of the ogre, but at the risk of falling to your death

Page.Text:
You dive out of the tree, your short sword in front of you, trying to hew the head off the ogre. It flinches as it sees you dive, and your sword strikes hard against its collarbone.
It throws your body back against the tree and flies into a rage. It shakes you and the tree so hard that the tree topples over, its roots flying up in a cloud of dirt, dust, and pine needles, and you fall down beside the tree.
What do you do?

Choice.text: Stand up and rush the ogre with your sword
Run for it

Page.Text:
You retreat into a particularly dense part of the forest, where the trees have grown close to one another. The ogre brings its club down on you, but it strikes a tree branch, which slams into you instead. You stab the ogre but its hide is so thick you don’t even draw blood.
What do you do?

Choice.text: Try to evade the club and get in close

Page.Text:
You stay absolutely still against the tree trunk, which is swaying slightly from your weight and a quickening breeze. The ogre has thrown its head back and is inhaling deeply. It leaves the path, and you lose sight of it among the trees. You can hear it snuffling somewhere beneath you.
The branch you are standing on is beginning to crack. It is getting sticky and slippery from the pine sap, as are your hands on the tree trunk.
What do you do?

Choice.text: Try to stay still and secure as long as possible, until eventually the branch cracks
Clamber up, hugging the tree, until your hands are so slick from sap that you hurt yourself sliding down a few branches

Page.Text:
When you left the healer, he warned you not to leave the path of the forest, but getting lost seems better than getting killed by an ogre.
You tried to stay off the trail, at the risk of encountering the ogre again. But you tried to stay near enough to the trail that you would not lose it.
Unfortunately, the advice of the healer was wise, and at some point you lost sight of the trail and could not find it again. You wandered through the forest, growing more and more desperate as the day advanced, until finally in late afternoon you rediscovered the trail.
Your arrow thunks into the shoulder of the ogre, bouncing harmless off it. The ogre rushes you, surprisingly quickly. It is swinging its club at you.

Choice.text: Try to roll under its swinging club to come close enough to stab it
Use your bow to defend yourself from taking the full force of the club

Page.Text:
When you left the healer, he warned you not to leave the path of the forest, but getting lost seems better than getting killed by an ogre.
What do you do?

Choice.text: Trust what you saw from the treetop—strike out east, confident that you will reach the trail further on, at the risk of taking too much time
Try to stay off the trail but near it, at the risk of encountering the ogre again

Page.Text:
You slowly and carefully climb down the tree, then step out on the path. “Hello!” you call out. “So nice to see you!”
The ogre wipes a tear from its eye and glares at you.
“Don’t mind me. I’m just walking through the woods. I’ll be out of your way in a moment. Is there anything I can do for you first? Something bothering you?”
“No have gift for Ugromsh on her day.”
What do you do?

Choice.text: Try to think of everything you’ve heard about ogres and figure out what Ugromsh might want
Offer it a gift but establish leverage over it first
Offer the ogre a gift in exchange for passing by, but add +1 forward to your roll.

Page.Text:
Your brown leather scabbard was adorned with wavy patterns that made it easier to blend in with the fallen brown leaves and pine needles. You were confident that the ogre would not see it from the path.
What do you do?

Choice.text: Search among the piles of leaves along the trail for as long as it takes
Forget the sword and travel along the path

Page.Text:
You drop your bow and roll under the club to get in range to stab the ogre. You whip out your sword, but the ogre drops its club and tries to crush you with its meaty hands.
What do you do?

Choice.text: Try to hamstring it
Try to cut off its hand

Page.Text:
It is hard to hold yourself tight against the tree trunk and shoot at the same time. Even worse, the dense branches of the tree, which made it so easy for you to climb, make it hard for you to line up a good shot.
Choose one (whichever you choose you deal your damage):

Choice.text: Climb down a branch or two, closer to it, for a clear shot
Shoot from where you are and take what you get
Loose arrow after arrow, spending what is left in the quiver

Page.Text:
Your sword in front of you, you retreat into a particularly dense part of the forest, where the trees have grown close to one another. The ogre brings its club down on you, but it strikes a tree branch, which slams into you instead.
What do you do?

Choice.text: Turn and run through the woods as quickly as you can
Retreat even deeper into the thicket behind you

Page.Text: You stride off, leaving the ogre cackling over the loot you gave it, then break into a run down the path.

Choice.text: Run for home
Run for home

Page.Text:
Your arrow strikes a branch then careens into the head of the ogre, but does no damage.
Roaring, the ogre begins shaking the tree even more forcefully.
What do you do?

Choice.text: Climb higher into the tree
Fire again

Page.Text:
As you drop from the tree, you see the ogre is rushing along the trail towards you, swinging its club before it like a scythe.
What do you do?

Choice.text: Notch an arrow to your bow and shoot it
Try to evade the swinging club and dart in close to the ogre
Retreat back into the pine trees, defending yourself as you do so

Page.Text:
When you left the healer, he warned you not to leave the path of the forest, but getting lost seems better than getting killed by an ogre.
What do you do?

Choice.text: Try to stay off the trail but near it, at the risk of hurting yourself among the rocks and branches of the forest floor
Strike off from the trail in the general direction of home, at the risk of taking so much time to get home that your sister has died before you can get her the healing potion

Page.Text:
You manage to avoid the swinging club and get in close to the ogre, your sword ready.
What do you do?

Choice.text: Strike with your sword
Try to hamstring it

Page.Text:
The dense branches of the tree, which made it so easy for you to climb, make it hard for you to line up a good shot.
Choose one (whichever you choose you deal your damage):

Choice.text: You have to move to get the shot, climbing down the tree and closer to the ogre, but dealing damage
You have to take what you can get
You have to shoot again and again, until there is nothing left to shoot, but you deal damage

Page.Text:
You have placed everything you still have into a pile, except for the healing potion. You start to place it into the pile with everything else. The eyes of the ogre widen, and it reaches out towards it.
What do you do?

Choice.text: Leave the potion and run. If you leave this, your sister will die, but you will live.
Hold onto the potion and run down the trail as fast as you can

Page.Text: The ogre tries to hide under one of the large branches. You fire again! Choose one:

Choice.text: You have to move to get the shot, climbing down within reach of the ogre, but dealing damage
You have to take what you can get
You have to shoot again and again, until there is nothing left to shoot, but you deal damage

Page.Text:
You stare at all your worldly possessions, placed before the ogre, but you look at the healing potion.
What do you do?

Choice.text: Leave the potion and run. If you leave this, your sister will die, but you will live.
Hold onto the potion and run down the trail as fast as you can

Page.Text:
You rush at the ogre through a cloud of dust and pine needles, driving your sword into its belly.
Grunting and bleeding, the ogre seizes you by the swordhand, crushing it. You scream in agony. The ogre pulls you up to it, then it takes a huge bite out of your left shoulder.
The ogre drops your apparently lifeless body to the ground and pulls your sword out of its belly, then falls to the ground.

You slump under the log, eyes closed, your backpack to one side. You feel the backpack being pulled off you, and hear the ogre open it. A few moments later you hear chewing. The ogre must be eating your rations. The log is pressed hard against your right leg, which is starting to ache.
Then you hear the ogre taking items out of the backpack. From the sounds of metal on metal, it seems like it’s going through your adventuring gear. Which means all that is left in your backpack is the healing potion that your sister needs.
You open your eyes just a bit. You can see the ogre looking at the spikes you carried in your pack. The pack is beside him, the sword on the other side of the pack away from him.
What do you do?

Choice.text: Lunge for the pack, then run for it
Lunge for the sword, then grab the pack

Page.Text:
You drop your bow and try to roll under the club to stab the ogre. But the ogre moves surprisingly quickly for its size, and it is well skilled with its club. It strikes a glancing blow; it could have been far worse. It raises its club to strike again.
What do you do?

Choice.text: Stab the ogre with your blade
Prepare to block the club with the flat of your sword

Page.Text:
The closely packed trees make it harder for the ogre to keep you at bay, enabling you to get close without being struck by the club. But these close trees don’t give you much room to maneuver either.
What do you do?

Choice.text: Attack with your sword
Try to hamstring it

Page.Text:
The branch you are standing on snaps with a loud crack, and you jump to another branch and throw your arms around the tree trunk, steadying yourself. You hear a roar from the ogre, which must have heard the breaking branch.
Your hands are slimy with sap, and you begin trying to brush the sap off on your clothes.
To your horror you hear the ogre coming closer. It is beneath you now and has begun shaking the tree violently.
What do you do?

Choice.text: Cling tightly to the tree so you don’t fall off to your death
Hold tightly to the tree but try to shoot the ogre with your bow

Page.Text:
As you run down the trail, you grow more and more tired. Night falls, and the darkness makes it hard to follow the trail; you must proceed slowly and carefully. When you run out of the woods and into the grasslands, a glimmer of moonlight at least helps you find your way.
You make it back to your family’s hut with the moon high in the sky. Your mother is slumped beside your sister’s bed. You rush to your sister’s side. Her hand is cold and stiff. You are too late.
The End.

Desperately you use your bow to try and stop the club from slamming down on you. The club knocks your bow from your hands and crushes your shoulder.
You unsheathe your sword and stab the ogre but its hide is so thick you don’t even draw blood.
The ogre raises the club to strike again.
What do you do?

Choice.text: Try to evade the club and get in close

Page.Text:
You recall campfire stories of the ogres. Ogres were once human, but they withdrew into the deep woods and to the tops of the high hills and found dark gods to worship. Ugromsh is one of those dark gods, a goddess of war, and she can be honored with gifts of bloodied weapons, as the ogres make no weapons for themselves.
What do you do?

Choice.text: Offer the ogre your sword as a gift to Ugromsh
Offer the ogre your bow and arrows as a gift to Ugromsh
Show it your empty hands: you have nothing left to give

Page.Text:
You are ready to curse the craftsmanship of the leather scabbard, when you suddenly catch sight of its wavy patterns. At last, you have it back in your hand. You can’t help but admire the filigree.
You hear the crunch of a branch breaking underfoot and hear the ogre off the trail somewhere near.

You pivot and plunge your blade into the rear of its leg, above the knee. Black blood spurts everywhere but the ogre is still upright.
What do you do?

Choice.text: Attack again and try to kill it
Run for it

Page.Text: You run as quickly as you can down the forest path. Suddenly the tree-trunk club of the ogre swings in front of you. You nimbly duck under it and continue running along the path, the roar of the ogre echoing behind you.

You turn to run through the woods but the ogre flies into a rage. The ogre jumps towards you, grabs your arm, twists it out of its socket, and pulls it out of your body. Then it begins pummeling you with it as you pass out from the pain and shock.

You climb the tree as high as you can, clinging tightly to the trunk. The top of the tree sways back and forth dramatically as the ogre shakes the tree.

Page.Text:
You spend an awkward moment reaching into your gear to untangle and pull out your rope. Then you give the rope, rations, and—last of all—your sword, to the ogre.
You back away slowly, leaving the ogre cackling over these items, then break into a run down the path.

Choice.text: Run for home
Run for home

Page.Text:
You pivot your body and kick repeatedly at the ogre’s arm with both your legs, trying to break free.
What do you do?

Choice.text: Push yourself so violently that you will hit the ground hard but away from the ogre
Land gently but within range of the ogre

Page.Text: You try to duck in close to stab the ogre, but it slams you hard with its club.

You let the sword go flying. You try to land in a soft patch of leaves and pine needles.
You come down safely in the leaves and even manage to keep your footing.
The ogre swings its club between you and your sword and is ready to smash you with it.
What do you do?

Choice.text: Make a run for it, leaving your sword behind
Try to roll under the club to grab your sword and get close to the ogre

Page.Text:
You’re confident that if you can just get close enough to the ogre you can kill it, but the ogre is determined to keep you at bay.
What do you do?

Choice.text: Dive in close despite the risk of being hit by the heavy club
Live and let live: run for it

Page.Text:
You throw your sword to the ground towards the ogre, drop to your knees and begin crawling under a thick branch. The ogre brings its club down on the branch. The branch breaks and slams into your back.
You crawl out from under the tree and break into a run. The ogre roars and follows, as you dodge in and out of the trees, heading back to the path. You run as quickly as your wounds will let you.
That isn’t very quickly, but fortunately the ogre runs even more slowly.

The ogre tries to slam you away from it using the club, but you square yourself to stand firm.
You plunge your sword back into its thigh. With a sigh, the ogre slides to the ground, and you slump beside it, too exhausted to crawl out of its reach.
You rest, listening to your breath, listening for—but not hearing—any breath from the ogre.You reach over and search its loincloth, reluctantly, but you find rations and a gem worth 400 coins.

You push yourself so hard that you arch backwards and slam into a rock on the ground.
You turn and crawl away even as the club slams into the ground near you. Jumping up, you toddle away, barely able to jog. You hear the clomps of the ogre behind you as it follows, but once you make it back to the trail you trot more quickly. Finally, you no longer hear its footsteps behind you.

Even as you try to make a run for it, the ogre’s club slams down on you, crushing you into the pile of leaves.
The ogre is drawing the club back to try and hammer you into your grave.
What do you do?

Choice.text: Roll out of the way and run for it
Grab your bow to use to defend yourself against the club

Page.Text: The ogre bellows as you turn and run back to the trail. The bellow is a mixture of pain and anger. You hear it stomping behind you, but you easily outdistance it, and keep running steadily. When you finally dare to look back, it is far behind you on the trail.
You rush the ogre, trying to catch it flat-footed, then break to the right and try to run past it. Out of the corner of your eye you saw the club come at you. You see stars and all goes black.

“Let me walk freely, and I will leave you to nurse your wounds and live another day,” you say.
The ogre’s only answer is to swing its club into your chest. You stagger back and nearly fall to the ground, but you keep your balance and step back towards the ogre.
What do you do?

Choice.text: Run for it
Try to kill the beast, without dying in the attempt

Page.Text:
You manage to somersault and land upright, only for the ogre’s club to barrel into you.
You’re dead before your body even hits the ground.

You try to dodge the club, but the ogre hits you dead on, knocking you back. You stumble but keep your feet.
What do you do?

Choice.text: Try to evade the club and get close enough to attack the ogre
Retreat back to the trail

Page.Text:
The ogre is in a frenzy, foam curling around its lips as it snarls. It’s waving the tree trunk back and forth to keep you from getting near, even as you try to dart in with your sword.
What do you do?

Choice.text: Fall back and run for it
Turn and take the club to your back but hold on to the sword

Page.Text: Even as you roll, the ogre brings its club down on you like a hammer.

You stagger forward and strike the ogre with your sword. Barely a nick against its thick hide.
The ogre drops its club and grabs hold of your head with one hand. You see red, then black.

You rush the ogre, even as it tries to strike you with its club. You turn your back to take the brunt of the blow.
What do you do?

Choice.text: Pivot and strike with your sword
Try to retreat out of range of the club

Page.Text:
You hold the two pieces of the broken bow together to fend off the worst of the ogre’s strike. The broken bow is worse than useless. The club slams into the pieces, sending them flying, and knocks off your feet, back out of range of the ogre.
What do you do?

Choice.text: Third time's a charm—try to evade the club and strike
Retreat and head home

Page.Text:
You pivot to try and drive your sword into the ogre’s thigh. Its skin is thick and scarred and your blade bounces off, and you shift back a step.
The ogre drives its club into your chest. You go flying and strike the branches of a tree, the force so strong it breaks the branches.

You roll, grab your blow, and catch enough of the club that you don’t feel the full force of it, even as it breaks your bow in half.
What do you do?

Choice.text: Roll out of range of the club and then run for it
Stagger to your feet, defending yourself with the doubled-up parts of the bow

Page.Text:
You notice a rhythm to how the ogre is swinging its club, and you do a sidestep and dance up next to the ogre, your sword at the ready. You go for the death blow.
Panicked, near death, the ogre grabs your swordhand, crushing it. The ogre throws your body far from it. You hit the ground hard.
Clouds seem to be moving in, for it is growing dark, as you lie in pain, watching the ogre as it watches you.

Even as you try to retreat to safety, avoiding the club, the ogre strikes you hard with the end of the tree trunk.
You go flying, doubled over, and everything goes black as you hit the ground.

Warily you rise to your feet. You are beaten and battered, but a sudden burst of adrenaline causes you to run as quickly as you can away from the ogre.
You hear no sound of pursuit from your severely wounded enemy.
Once the adrenaline wears off, you can’t run far. You stagger down the trail, first at a jog, then a swift pace, then walking as fast as you can.

You spread your hands. There is nothing on you that a goddess of war would want, and nothing on you worth the walk home.
The ogre looks at your empty hands for a long moment. Then it swings.
